newsitem.title: FRANCE: Germans discussing Algerian gas supplies.
newsitem.headline: Germans discussing Algerian gas supplies.

text.p: Germany is discussing the possible purchases of gas from Algeria, which within the next two or three weeks will put on stream a pipeline to supply Spain and Portugal, a visiting German minister said on Monday.

German junior foreign minister Werner Hoyer told a news conference in Algiers, winding up a three day visit: "We are very interested in Algerian gas. The outlook for this is important. Our talks with Sonatrach have focused on this subject."

Sonatrach is Algeria's state-owned oil and gas giant which has recently completed a pipeline running from Hassi R'mel in the Sahara desert to take gas to Spain, Portugal and possibly later to France and other markets.
It is expected to come on stream early next month.
OPEC member Algeria currently exports some 30 billion cubic metres of gas a year, mostly to Europe, and has a gas pipeline running to Italy. It plans to double its gas exports by the year 2000.

Hoyer, whose remarks were carried on Algerian radio, said Germany was setting up a joint company with the state-run vehicle producer Societe Nationale des Vehicules Industriels and the German firm DIAG.
The firm, backed by German capital, would produce machines to replace worn out machinery in Algeria's industrial sector.
Hoyer also said Germany was interested in Algeria's banking and financial sector and could look at setting up a German bank in the North African country.
